extra.message: Affected versions of python-multipart are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. An attacker can cause uncontrolled CPU consumption (denial of service) by sending a small application/x-www-form-urlencoded body that uses ";" as the field separator. python-multipart's QuerystringParser performs a full failed scan for "&" over the entire remaining buffer before locating each ";", resulting in quadratic-time parsing.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CWE-407: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
metadata.license: Semgrep Rules License v1.0. For more details, visit semgrep.dev/legal/rules-license

extra.message: Affected versions of python-multipart are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. python-multipart's MultipartParser enforced no limits on the number or size of part headers, so a network attacker can send a multipart/form-data body with many or oversized part headers to keep the parser in its header state machine and burn CPU before the request is rejected. Any code that instantiates MultipartParser/FormParser or calls parse_form/create_form_parser to handle multipart bodies is reachable to this DoS.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Affected versions of starlette are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Serving static files with Starlette's StaticFiles app on Windows resolves requested paths with os.path.realpath() before checking directory containment. A request for a UNC path (e.g. \\attacker.com\share) triggers an outbound SMB connection, letting an unauthenticated attacker perform server-side request forgery and leak the service account's NTLMv2 credentials.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
metadata.sca-reachable-if: you run the application on Windows
metadata.license: Semgrep Rules License v1.0. For more details, visit semgrep.dev/legal/rules-license

extra.message: Affected versions of starlette are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Calling `request.form()` parses `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies without enforcing the `max_fields` or `max_part_size` limits, so an unauthenticated attacker can send a request with an extremely large number of fields or an oversized field value to exhaust CPU/memory and cause a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification). urllib3 fails to enforce its decompression-bomb safeguards in two streaming-API code paths: (1) the second and subsequent HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) or HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N) calls on a Brotli-encoded response, and (2) HTTPResponse.drain_conn() invoked after the body has been partially decompressed. A malicious server can return a highly compressed payload to force the client to fully decompress it in a single operation, consuming excessive CPU and memory.

cwe: CWE-409: Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)
metadata.license: Semgrep Rules License v1.0. For more details, visit semgrep.dev/legal/rules-license

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. HTTP pools obtained from urllib3 ProxyManager via connection_from_url() or connection_from_host() do not strip sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization) when following cross-origin redirects, leaking authentication credentials to the redirect target. Use ProxyManager.request() (the high-level API) instead, or upgrade to urllib3 >= 2.7.0.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
